headline: From Rejection to Revolution: Africa's First Women-Owned Pad Factory
meta_description: An investor's dismissal sparked a breakthrough. Now Africa's first women-owned sanitary pad factory produces 800 pads per minute and serves over 100,000 people.
summary_short: Told she didn't fit the investor profile, one woman built Africa's first women-owned sanitary pad factory—now producing 800 pads a minute.
body:
An investor told her she "didn't fit the profile." Rather than accept that rejection, she built Africa's first women-owned sanitary pad factory.

Today, the operation runs with remarkable scale: the factory produces 800 pads per minute, transforming what could have been a setback into a thriving enterprise. Beyond the production numbers lies a deeper mission—the factory provides free sanitary products to more than 100,000 people, addressing a critical gap in menstrual health access across the continent.

Her story challenges the gatekeeping that women entrepreneurs often face in finance and manufacturing. What an investor dismissed as an unlikely candidate turned into a leader solving a real problem at real speed.
quick_facts: Africa's first women-owned sanitary pad factory
Provides free products to over 100,000 people
